AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.error: Judges soil quality by colour alone (thinks dark soil is poor and pale soil is rich).

example.question: Which soil is likely to be poor for growing crops?
example.wrong_answer: Dark, crumbly soil full of rotted leaves
example.correct_answer: Pale, hard soil with no plants and gullies

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.cause: The child links dark with dirty or burnt and pale with clean.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.reveals: Offer "Dark, crumbly soil full of rotted leaves" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.help: Show two soils: dark crumbly and pale packed. Ask which holds water and which grows a seed, then ask what the colour tells.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.feedback: Colour alone does not tell. Dark, crumbly soil is usually rich in rotted plant matter. Bare, hard, washed-away ground is a sign of poor soil.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.error: Digs the waste pit anywhere (in a hollow where rain collects, or beside the borehole).

example.question: Where is the best place for the school organic waste pit?
example.wrong_answer: In the low place where rain water collects
example.correct_answer: On firm higher ground near the garden, away from the well

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.cause: The child thinks wet ground helps waste to rot and does not think about drinking water.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.reveals: Offer "In the low place where rain water collects" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.help: Walk the site after rain. Ask what happens to a pit that fills with water, and what could happen to a nearby well.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.feedback: A pit in a hollow floods and a pit near drinking water can pollute it. Choose firm ground near the garden and away from the well.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

review.mark: plausible, to confirm by a teacher
review.note: Own judgement: believable for a Kenyan child of this age, but we have no source or homework count. A teacher who knows the class should say whether children really hold it.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.error: Thinks a bare patch is just normal ground that needs no help.

example.question: The playground edge is hard and bare and crops there turn yellow and stay small. What is this a sign of?
example.wrong_answer: The ground is normal and needs nothing
example.correct_answer: The soil is poor and needs improving

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.cause: The child has seen bare ground all their life and does not read it as a problem.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.reveals: Offer "The ground is normal and needs nothing" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.help: Plant the same seed in a bare patch and in the garden and compare after two weeks.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.feedback: Hard bare ground and small yellow crops show the soil is poor. It needs rotted plant matter and manure to improve it.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

review.mark: doubtful
review.why: Children see bare hard ground where nothing grows and know it is poor; a trap option.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.error: Puts any rubbish in the organic waste pit (polythene, tins, glass).

example.question: Which of these should NOT go into an organic waste pit?
example.correct_answer: Banana peelings

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.cause: The child thinks a pit is a general rubbish pit.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.error: Thinks cooked food, meat and bones are good for the pit.

example.wrong_answer: They are the best food for the pit
example.correct_answer: They draw rats and flies and smell

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.reveals: Offer "They are the best food for the pit" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.feedback: Meat and oily leftovers draw rats and flies. Peelings, leaves, grass and dung are better.

example.question: After the pit is filled, what should the school do?
example.wrong_answer: Leave it dry and open for the whole year
example.correct_answer: Keep it damp and covered and wait for it to rot

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.cause: The child thinks rotting happens by itself.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.reveals: Offer "Leave it dry and open for the whole year" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.error: Thinks burning plant remains is the best way to clear them.

example.correct_answer: The humus and plant food the stalks would have given

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.feedback: Burning wastes the plant matter. Rotted stalks give the soil humus and plant food.

review.mark: plausible, to confirm by a teacher

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.error: Calls plant remains rubbish with no use.

example.question: What is a good use of the leaves and grass cleared from the school compound?
example.wrong_answer: Throw them away on the road
example.correct_answer: Make compost or spread them as mulch

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.cause: The child sees cleared leaves as waste to get rid of.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.reveals: Offer "Throw them away on the road" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.help: Ask where forest soil gets its food from, then link to fallen leaves.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.feedback: Leaves and grass can be rotted into compost or used as mulch. They are plant food in waiting.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.error: Thinks soil where weeds grow thickly is always poor and needs improving.

example.question: Thick green weeds grow in one corner of the school. What does this say about the soil?
example.correct_answer: The soil there is likely fertile and moist

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.cause: The child sees weeds as a sign of a neglected, bad place.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.reveals: Offer "The soil there is poor" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.help: Compare the weedy corner with a bare hard patch: which soil is dark and soft when dug?
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.feedback: Plants grow thickly where the soil is good. Bare, hard or washed patches need improving.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.SOIL_SI.source: To confirm by a CBC Agriculture teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.error: Thinks the deeper the pit, the better, even if it fills with water.

example.question: Why is an organic waste pit not dug in a waterlogged place?
example.wrong_answer: Water helps the waste rot faster
example.correct_answer: The pit fills with water, the waste rots badly and smells

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.cause: The child knows rotting needs water and does not see that too much water stops air reaching it.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.reveals: Offer "Water helps the waste rot faster" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.help: Compare a jar of leaves just damp with one under water after two weeks: smell and look.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.feedback: Waste rots well when damp, not soaked. A pit in wet ground floods and smells.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.COMPOST.source: To confirm by a CBC Agriculture teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.error: Thinks fresh plant remains feed the crop the moment they are put on the soil.

example.question: Maize stalks are laid on the soil. When do they feed the soil?
example.correct_answer: Slowly, as they rot over weeks and months

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.cause: The child thinks of plant remains like fertiliser poured on.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.reveals: Offer "At once, the same day" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.help: Look at mulch laid last term: what has happened to the bottom layer?
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.feedback: Plant remains feed the soil slowly as they rot. Meanwhile they cover and protect it.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.source: To confirm by a CBC Agriculture teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.error: Thinks plant remains are only good as animal feed and give the soil nothing.

example.question: Which is a use of plant remains for soil improvement?
example.correct_answer: Using them as mulch or compost

AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.cause: In many homes stover goes to the animals, so the child sees no other use.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.reveals: Offer "Only feeding them to cattle" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.help: Ask what happens to the soil under a mulch of dry grass in the dry season.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.feedback: Plant remains can be mulch or compost. They keep water in and add humus to the soil.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.SOIL_CONSERVATION.PLANT_R.source: To confirm by a CBC Agriculture teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.error: Thinks midday is the best time to water because it is hot and the plants are thirsty.

example.question: When is it best to water a garden to save water?
example.wrong_answer: At midday when the sun is hottest
example.correct_answer: Early in the morning or in the evening

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.cause: The child links heat with thirst.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.reveals: Offer "At midday when the sun is hottest" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.help: Pour a cup of water on the ground at noon and one at six in the evening and compare how long each stays damp.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.feedback: In the heat much of the water dries off before it soaks in. Water early or late.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

review.mark: plausible, to confirm by a teacher
review.note: Own judgement: believable for a Kenyan child of this age, but we have no source or homework count. A teacher who knows the class should say whether children really hold it.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.error: Thinks mulch is for keeping plants warm or for feeding them, not for keeping water in.

example.question: What does a layer of dry grass around kale do for the water in the soil?
example.wrong_answer: It keeps the plants warm at night
example.correct_answer: It slows the drying of the soil

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.cause: The child knows a cover keeps something warm.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.reveals: Offer "It keeps the plants warm at night" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.help: Uncover a mulched patch and a bare patch at midday and feel both.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.feedback: Mulch shades the soil so water dries off slowly. That is how it saves water.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

review.mark: plausible, to confirm by a teacher
review.note: Own judgement: believable for a Kenyan child of this age, but we have no source or homework count. A teacher who knows the class should say whether children really hold it.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.error: Thinks the only way to help a dry garden is to use more water.

example.question: A garden dries out quickly. Which action saves water?
example.wrong_answer: Pouring much more water on it each day
example.correct_answer: Covering the soil with a layer of dry grass

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.cause: The child links dry with more water.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.reveals: Offer "Pouring much more water on it each day" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.help: Ask where the water went. Then show that a cover stops it escaping.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.feedback: More water can simply dry off or run away. A mulch, a cover crop or shade keeps the water in the soil.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

review.mark: doubtful
review.why: Children know mulch and shade keep a bed moist; "more water only" is mostly a trap option.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.error: Changes more than one thing in a test (different crop or different water).

example.question: To test mulch, Otieno gives the mulched bed less water and plants beans there and kale in the other bed. What is wrong?
example.wrong_answer: Nothing is wrong, this is fair
example.correct_answer: More than one thing differs, so the result tells nothing

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.cause: The child wants to help the mulched bed or does not know what a fair test is.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.reveals: Offer "Nothing is wrong, this is fair" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.help: Ask what Otieno could blame if the mulched bed did better.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.feedback: A fair test changes only one thing. Same crop, same soil and same water, with and without mulch.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.error: Expects the mulched bed to dry faster.

example.question: After a week of sun, which bed will stay damp longer, the mulched one or the bare one?
example.correct_answer: The mulched one

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.cause: The child thinks a cover traps heat and dries soil.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.reveals: Offer "The bare one" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.help: Do the test: dig a finger deep in both beds and feel.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.feedback: Mulch shades the soil and slows drying, so the mulched bed stays damp longer.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

review.mark: doubtful
review.why: Children who have felt wet mulched soil expect it to stay damp; a trap option.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.error: Thinks used washing water can never be used in the garden.

example.question: Which water can be reused on garden plants?

example.correct_answer: Water left after washing vegetables or rinsing, without strong soap

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.cause: The child thinks used water is dirty and harmful to everything.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.reveals: Offer "None, garden water must be fresh" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.help: Pour vegetable-washing water on a bed and watch the plants over a week.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.feedback: Water from washing vegetables can water the garden. Do not use water with strong soap or bleach.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.WATER_.source: To confirm by a CBC Agriculture teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.error: Judges the soil only by its top crust, so the bare bed looks as damp as the mulched one after rain.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.reveals: Offer "Look at the top of the soil" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.help: Dig a finger into both beds two days after watering: the bare one is dry below the crust.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.feedback: Feel a few centimetres down. The top can look damp while the soil below is dry.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.source: To confirm by a CBC Agriculture teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.error: Reads the result after one day and calls it final.

example.question: When should the results of a mulching test be read?

AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.feedback: A fair test needs time. Check every day for several days before you decide.
AGRI.G5.CONSER.WATER_CONSERVATION.MULCH_.source: To confirm by a CBC Agriculture teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.wrong_answer: A scarecrow made of old clothes
